goal: Compare post-hoc hard-node calibration/threshold policies without training a new model.

headline.decision: Do not promote benchmark-tuned or shrinkage threshold policies based on this limited diagnostic run.

interpretation: Fixed 0.5 threshold is clearly invalid for the current hard head probabilities.
Class-tuned validation thresholds remain the correct evaluation policy.
Benchmark-tuned and benchmark-shrinkage thresholds did not improve hard F1 in the limited run.
Next useful work should focus on probability calibration, class-boundary training, and wider benchmark coverage before adding action-ranking loss.
limitations: This was a CPU diagnostic run with max_val_samples=512 and max_steps=128.
The sampled validation subset had limited benchmark coverage, so results are diagnostic and not a full 5-seed validation claim.
next_recommended_autoresearch_goal: Design and run a wider calibration diagnostic across more validation benchmarks, then decide whether to add calibration loss or temperature scaling.
